posts.post_subject: New source for LCD screens for Stereograms
posts.content_md:
I have been thinking about working on the poor mans liti hologram printer and I have noticed the digital picture frames have been getting cheaper and cheaper.

[http://www.circuitcity.com/ssm/Specific ... on.do#tabs](http://www.circuitcity.com/ssm/Specifications-of-Portable-USA-Digital-Picture-Frame-PU-10W/sem/rpsm/oid/178232/rpem/ccd/productDetailSpecification.do#tabs)

This one has resonable resolution. The question would be if one could remove the backlight without destroying the LCD. The only LCDs I have had appart just fell apart in my hands as soon as I had the screws out. Are some glued?

posts.post_subject: New source for LCD screens for Stereograms
posts.content_md:
Colin - 

I don't know the answer to your question, but I think a community that would be able to answer your question very quickly is that affiliated with the forums at Make magazine. It's a popular "DIY" group.

You probably already read it, but it's at [http://www.makezine.com](http://www.makezine.com). Just click on that "forum" link and ask away. I had questions about a digital photoframe for an art project and got a bunch of answers pretty quickly.

g

posts.post_subject: New source for LCD screens for Stereograms
posts.content_md: Can these LCD's be controlled through a USB port? I mean, is it possible to show a picture on command from the PC? This would be a requirement because otherwise there would be a timing problem with the stereo printer.

posts.topic_title: New source for LCD screens for Stereograms
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: New source for LCD screens for Stereograms
posts.content_md: The ones I have seen take a memory card and display all of the images with a pre-determined delay. I was thinking of loading one image at a time. Obviously time consuming but faster than indexing images off of film.
